adhd.label: Step 1 · Prologue: Families in Kolkata (Start Here — The Personal Mystery)
adhd.brief: Siddhartha Mukherjee travels with his father through Kolkata to visit his schizophrenic cousin Moni, asking how a tiny physical code inside our cells carries both brilliance and mental illness across generations.

adhd.label: Step 2 · Jumps to Part II: Seeing the 3D DNA Double Helix (Franklin, Crick & Watson)
adhd.brief: Jumps ahead to 1953 Cambridge and London, where Rosalind Franklin's X-ray photographs and Watson and Crick's brass models reveal the physical four-letter twisted staircase that copies all life.

adhd.label: Step 3 · Jumps Back to Part I: Mendel's Pea Garden (How Discrete Code Packets Work)
adhd.brief: Now that you can picture DNA, we jump back to Gregor Mendel cross-breeding 28,000 pea plants in his monastery garden to prove that traits pass from parent to child as unbreakable packets rather than blended fluids.

adhd.label: Step 4 · Jumps to Epilogue: Bheda, Abheda (Epigenetics, Fate & Human Freedom)
adhd.brief: Returns to the Mukherjee family and the modern CRISPR era, showing how environmental triggers flip genetic switches on and off and why understanding our genome liberates us from fatalism.
